lines.trans: Here we are at the municipal clock tower—and the shadow points straight to this park!

words.gram: def m sg noun with w- (and)

lines.trans: Let me read Card Three: Find the iron bench where the oldest linden tree drops its leaves.
That is easy; the oldest linden tree is right there in the centre.
And there is a green iron bench sitting perfectly in its shade!
Come on, let us see if there is another carved symbol waiting for us.
Wait—look at the wooden slats on the back of the bench!
There is a tiny star carved into the wood! We found the third clue!
Excellent! Card Three says: Open the small envelope when all four corners meet.
We only have three cards! Where is Card Four?
Did we drop it in the alley? No, wait—look at the back of Card Three!
It says: Card Four is always where you started.
We started at Jasmine Courtyard! Do we have to walk all the way back?!
Here we are at the municipal clock tower—and the shadow points straight to this park!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: I bought four books.
The guests arrived at four in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأشر, بيأشر).

examples.trans: Salma motioned to me from the kitchen.
Rami is pointing to the two chairs.

meanings.note: Elative comparative/superlative of قديم (old); invariable across gender and number.

examples.text: هاي أقدم شجرة زيتون بالحارة كلها.
examples.trans: This is the oldest olive tree in the whole neighbourhood.

examples.text: الكتاب هادا أقدم من كل الكتب اللي عالرف.
examples.trans: This book is older than every other book on the shelf.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun for 'we' (equivalent to formal نحن).

examples.trans: We respect all our guests.
We are ready for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: Form VIII defective verb; used both for people meeting and lines/corners meeting.

examples.text: الزوايا الأربعة بتلتقي بنقطة واحدة بالنص.
examples.trans: The four corners meet at a single point in the middle.

examples.text: التقينا عند برج الساعة قبل الغروب.
examples.trans: We met by the clock tower before sunset.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببدا, بيبدا).

examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.
The day began lively and bright.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical tower, a skyscraper, or an astrological sign.

examples.trans: This is the highest tower in the city.

examples.text: برج الساعة القديم مبين من فوق السطوح.
examples.trans: The old clock tower is visible from the rooftop.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: A highly versatile prefix used as a preposition of place or instrument.

examples.trans: We went to work by car.

examples.text: اكتب اسمك بـ قلم الحبر على البطاقة.
examples.trans: Write your name with the fountain pen on the card.

meanings.note: From بلد ('country, town'); prized on Jordanian market stalls for local olive oil, honey, lemons, and thyme.

examples.text: عسل بلدي من جبال عجلون ريحته بتشهي.
examples.trans: Local honey from the Ajloun hills smells delicious.
We bought yellow local lemons for tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تالتة, plural: تالتين).

examples.trans: The attic room is on the third floor.
He used to sit on the third step.

meanings.note: The number 3 when followed by a counted noun.

examples.trans: I have three cars in the garage.

examples.text: مشينا تلات دقايق وبعدين وصلنا عالبوابة.
examples.trans: We walked three minutes and then reached the gate.

meanings.note: The metal iron. Used commonly in construction contexts or metaphorically for strength.

examples.trans: This door is made of iron.

examples.text: قفل البوابة مصنوع من حديد قديم وتقيل.
examples.trans: The gate lock is made of old, heavy iron.

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian feminine noun for a public park or walled garden (حدائق 'parks').

examples.trans: The park bench is painted beside the arch.

examples.text: بنتمشى بالحديقة كل يوم جمعة العصر.
examples.trans: We walk in the park every Friday afternoon.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: This table is made of wood.

examples.text: الصندوق مصنوع من خشب جوز قديم وناعم.
examples.trans: The chest is made of smooth old walnut wood.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.
Stay calm, Mariam.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian speech, خيال commonly means a cast 'shadow' or 'silhouette' as well as 'imagination'.

examples.text: شفت خيال القطة على الحيط تحت الفانوس.
examples.trans: I saw the cat's shadow on the wall beneath the lantern.

examples.text: خيال الشجرة واصل لحد باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: The tree's shadow reaches right to the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of دائما ('always').

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.
Noon traffic is always slow.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Walk straight and then turn right.

examples.text: امشي دغري لعند القوس وبعدين لف يسار.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the arch and then turn left.

meanings.note: Can mean evidence, proof, or a guide (both a person and a guidebook).

examples.trans: Do you have evidence for what you're saying?

examples.text: هادا الرقم الصغير هو أول دليل للوصول للكنز.
examples.trans: This small number is the first clue for reaching the treasure.

meanings.note: Ordinal number from أربعة (four). Feminine: رابعة.

examples.text: البند الرابع عشر من قانون عمان القديمة.
examples.trans: Clause fourteen of the Amman Old Quarter Act.
This is the fourth cup of coffee today.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Refers to map symbols, emblems, or passwords.

examples.text: شو الرمز اللي لازم نلاقيه عالكرت الأول؟
examples.trans: What is the symbol that we need to find on the first card?
The jasmine tree is a symbol of hospitality in this house.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: Put the chair in the corner.
The chest is placed in the northern corner of the room.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزقة.

examples.trans: The stone alley is narrow and quiet.
We turned past the narrow lane.

meanings.note: Aromatic tree whose dried blossoms are brewed as soothing herbal tea across Jordan and the Levant.

examples.text: سعاد زرعت شجرة زيزفون جنب البوابة الشرقية.
examples.trans: Suad planted a linden tree beside the eastern gate.

examples.text: شاي الزيزفون الدافي بريح الأعصاب بالليل.
examples.trans: Warm linden tea soothes the nerves at night.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: I've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح كمان ساعة، خلينا نستنى بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The library opens in another hour; let us wait in the garden.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'easy to do'.

examples.text: هاي الوصفة سهلة وبتجهز بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: This recipe is easy and comes together in half an hour.

examples.text: سهل نرتب الكراسي بعد ما يخلص الدهان.
examples.trans: It will be easy to arrange the chairs once the painting is done.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tree.

examples.trans: We planted an olive tree in the garden.

examples.text: قعدنا تحت شجرة الزيزفون الكبيرة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We sat under the big linden tree in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.text: عندي أخ صغير عمره خمس سنين.
examples.trans: I have a young brother who is five years old.

examples.text: في مفتاح نحاس صغير مخبي تحت الورقة.
examples.trans: There is a small brass key hidden under the sheet.

meanings.note: Used in عالطريق ('on the way') and طول الطريق ('all the way').

examples.trans: The hot tea is on the way right now!
I repeated the sentence all along the way.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for shade under trees or an awning (تحت الظل 'in the shade'). Plural: ظلال.

examples.trans: We watched the sun behind the shade.
Sit in the shade, the weather is hot today.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

meanings.note: Literally 'sitting', but widely used as an auxiliary participle to denote continuous present action (like English '-ing').

examples.trans: I am (currently) studying for the exam.

examples.text: مازن قاعد بقرا التعليمات بصوت عالي عشان الكل يسمع.
examples.trans: Mazen is sitting reading the instructions aloud so everyone can hear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: All people love summer.

examples.text: كل بطاقة بالعلبة بتحكي عن نبتة عطرية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every card in the tin talks about a different aromatic plant.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.trans: I want tea, and also coffee.

examples.text: ذقنا التانية وكمان التالتة عشان نقارن القوام.
examples.trans: We tasted the second one and also the third to compare the texture.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, I don't want to go today.

examples.text: لا تنسوا تطفيوا الفرن بعد ما تخلصوا الخبيز.
examples.trans: Do not forget to turn off the oven after you finish baking.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

لاقى.gloss: to find; to encounter; to meet

meanings.en: to find; to encounter; to meet
meanings.note: Form III defective verb widely used in Jordanian Arabic as the everyday verb meaning to find (alongside لقي).

examples.text: أخيرا لاقينا المفتاح الضاع تحت السجادة.
examples.trans: We finally found the lost key under the rug.

examples.text: إذا دورت منيح بالدرج بتلاقي الكرت.
examples.trans: If you look carefully in the drawer you will find the card.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Form I defective verb (fa'il class: لقي / يلقى) used extensively in Jordanian speech for finding lost objects.

examples.text: لقينا ثلاث بطاقات قديمة جوا الكتاب.
examples.trans: We found three old cards inside the book.

examples.text: مازن لقي الوصفة الأصلية بخط جدته.
examples.trans: Mazen found the original recipe in his grandmother's handwriting.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Call me when you reach home.

examples.text: لما بردت الكيكة صبينا فوقها العسل الدافي.
examples.trans: When the cake cooled, we poured the warm honey over it.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Refers to a paper envelope used for letters or documents.

examples.trans: I put the money in an envelope.

examples.text: حطينا البطاقات كلها جوا مغلف ورق بني.
examples.trans: We put all the cards inside a brown paper envelope.

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: The name is written on the board.

examples.text: الرقم مكتوب بخط صغير تحت الختم الأحمر.
examples.trans: The number is written in small handwriting beneath the red seal.

meanings.note: Very common word of approval or rating something highly.

examples.trans: Your work is excellent today.

examples.text: توازن السكر والليمون بهاي الكيكة ممتاز جدا.
examples.trans: The balance of sugar and lemon in this cake is truly excellent.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Passive participle of نحت (to carve stone or wood); used for architectural reliefs and carved wooden items.

examples.text: في رقم منحوت على الحجر فوق البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a number carved into the stone above the gate.

examples.text: القوس المنحوت بالحيط قديم ومتقن كتير.
examples.trans: The carved arch in the wall is old and very finely crafted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موجودة, plural: موجودين).

examples.trans: Your glasses are right there on your forehead!
Tariq is down in the workshop.

meanings.note: Used for celestial stars, geometric shapes, or famous celebrities.

examples.trans: The sky is full of stars today.

examples.text: رسموا نجمة صغيرة بالحبر الأحمر جنب الرقم سبعة.
examples.trans: They drew a small star in red ink beside the number seven.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: The time is five and a half (half past five).

examples.text: التقينا بالساحة الساعة تمانية ونص تماما.
examples.trans: We met in the courtyard at eight-thirty sharp.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.text: هادا الكتاب من أحلى الروايات اللي قرأتها هالسنة.
examples.trans: This book is one of the best novels I've read this year.

examples.text: مين جاب هادا الفانوس الحلو عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Who brought this lovely lantern onto the table?

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine demonstrative adverb parallel to هناك (over there).

examples.text: اللوحة القديمة معلقة هنيك عند الدرج.
examples.trans: The old painting is hanging over there by the stairs.

examples.text: روحوا هنيك تحت شجرة الزيزفون الجو أبرد.
examples.trans: Go over there under the linden tree; it is cooler.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقع, بيوقع).

examples.text: نظارتك وقعت عن أنفك من الفرحة!
examples.trans: Your glasses fell off your nose for joy!

examples.text: أي نزل سحري هاد اللي وقعت فيه؟
examples.trans: What magical inn is this that you stumbled into?

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where are you going?

examples.text: وين حطيت مفاتيح السيارة بعد ما رجعت من الشغل؟
examples.trans: Where did you put the car keys after you got back from work?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Very common interjection used to urge action or to say goodbye ('yalla bye').

examples.trans: Come on let's go, we're late.

examples.text: يلا البس جاكيتك بسرعة، الأوبر صار واقف تحت.
examples.trans: Come on, put your jacket on quickly—the Uber is already waiting downstairs.
